name: Yaya Bey
label: Big Dada
lede: Her father told her not to sing. Yaya Bey put out three albums on Elevated anyway, signed to Big Dada, and ended 2022 at No. 9 on Pitchfork's year-end list.

eras.title: A rapper's daughter starts writing
eras.text: Yaya Bey grew up in New York, the daughter of Juice Crew rapper Grand Daddy I.U., and wrote her first songs as a kid. Three albums on Elevated followed, with a divorce and a move to New York in the middle.

years.src: Yaya Bey (Wikipedia) · Grand Daddy I.U. (Wikipedia) · Permanent Rotation
years.h: Hidaiyah Bey is born in Queens, a Cold Chillin' rapper's daughter
years.p: Her father is [[Grand Daddy I.U.|f807e647-ee9a-4b57-9729-250e13a28984]], the suit-and-tie Juice Crew rapper. According to The Vinyl Factory, he told her she could not and should not sing, and pushed her to write instead.
years.xp:
Ayub Bey signed to Cold Chillin' Records in 1989 after [[Biz Markie|48b48175-5ffd-49a2-88e2-ca84118544ca]] heard his demo, and his debut Smooth Assassin came out in 1990, according to Wikipedia.

She wrote poetry and songs from elementary school. Around 13 she found a Roberta Flack and Donny Hathaway record in her grandmother's basement.

years.src: In Conversation: Yaya Bey · Yaya Bey (Wikipedia)
years.h: The Many Alter-Egos of Trill'eta Brown goes out on Elevated
years.p: Clash lists it as her first project. It is where the name Yaya Bey first gets out into the world.
years.xp: It came four years before the press started paying attention.

years.src: In Conversation: Yaya Bey · Yaya Bey (Wikipedia)
years.h: A divorce in progress, and This Too... gets made
years.p: The second Elevated album. Bey told Clash the marriage was ending while she made it.
years.xp: She called the divorce process "way too traumatic to be invested in." The record came out before Madison Tapes.

years.src: In Conversation: Yaya Bey · SPOTLIGHT: Yaya Bey
years.h: Bey leaves D.C. for New York with no job and no house
years.p: Clash dates the move to April 2019. Big Dada had already called that year, but the timing wasn't right.
years.xp:
Bey told Clash she arrived "unemployed" and "houseless." "I lost a whole life. I had friends, I lived in a house."

Of the label that would sign her two years later: "They give me advice; they give me resources and they let me do what I feel I need to do."

Sources differ on her early years: Wikipedia and The Luna Collective place her upbringing in Queens, while Clash covers her earlier stretch in D.C.

eras.title: Big Dada picks her up
eras.text: Madison Tapes is the record she says found her sound. Big Dada, which first called in 2019, relaunches her with an EP the next year.

years.src: In Conversation: Yaya Bey · Interview: Yaya Bey Came Here to Live
years.h: She finds her sound on Madison Tapes
years.p: Released on Elevated. Bey told Clash it changed how she approached albums, and Range calls it her breakthrough.
years.xp: Clash says she made it deeply depressed and working 13-hour days. Wikipedia dates the start of her professional music career to this album, though she had already released three on Elevated.

years.cap: Yaya Bey at Hopscotch Music Festival, Raleigh, N.C., Sept. 9, 2022
years.src: In Conversation: Yaya Bey · Yaya Bey (Wikipedia)
years.h: Big Dada relaunches her with The Things I Can't Take with Me
years.p: The EP follows two years of conversations with the label. Pitchfork, Rolling Stone and The Guardian all reviewed it.

eras.title: North Star
eras.text: Her Big Dada debut album lands in June and ends the year at No. 9 on Pitchfork's list. In December her father dies.

years.cap: Yaya Bey at Hopscotch Music Festival, Raleigh, N.C., Sept. 9, 2022
years.src: In Conversation: Yaya Bey · Yaya Bey (Wikipedia)
years.h: Pitchfork gives Remember Your North Star an 8.6
years.p: Eighteen tracks, opened by "Keisha" and co-produced by Bey with [[Aja Grant|75f15961-340a-4619-9c4a-0002469fb729]] of Phony Ppl and [[DJ Nativesun|b4efd9e0-6754-45a0-8f82-99f7575d54ce]]. Pitchfork's year-end list puts it at No. 9.
years.xp:
Album of the Year lists it at No. 9 on Pitchfork's 50 Best Albums of 2022, No. 14 at BrooklynVegan and No. 32 at The Guardian.

Bey called the record her thesis: in her words to BrooklynVegan, we do want love of self and love from our community. The Vinyl Factory quotes Pitchfork's Eric Torres on how it braids confidence and vulnerability.

years.big: "The whole concept of a North Star just feels more sure of itself."
years.src: Permanent Rotation · In Conversation: Yaya Bey
years.h: It was going to be called Safe Travels
years.p: Bey on why she renamed her album, speaking to The Vinyl Factory. Clash also lists Safe Travels as the original title.
years.xp:
Bey told Clash she arrived "unemployed" and "houseless." "I lost a whole life. I had friends, I lived in a house."

Of the label that would sign her two years later: "They give me advice; they give me resources and they let me do what I feel I need to do."

Sources differ on her early years: Wikipedia and The Luna Collective place her upbringing in Queens, while Clash covers her earlier stretch in D.C.

years.p: Ayub Bey, who recorded as [[Grand Daddy I.U.|f807e647-ee9a-4b57-9729-250e13a28984]], died on this date; Wikipedia gives no cause. He appears on his daughter's next album, Ten Fold.

eras.title: Grief, then a new label
eras.text: An EP, a 16-track Big Dada album shaped by her father's death, then two records on Drink Sum Wtr. The reviews keep coming.

years.h: An EP, Exodus the North Star, follows within the year
years.p: Wikipedia lists it as a 2023 Big Dada EP and gives no more. BBC Music filmed her playing the title song at Glastonbury that June.

years.cap: Yaya Bey at Øyafestivalen, Oslo, Aug. 10, 2024
q: I don't want to be my work. I want time to really be present.
years.src: Ten Fold (Wikipedia) · Interview: Yaya Bey Came Here to Live
years.h: Pitchfork calls Ten Fold Best New Music, 8.4
years.p: Sixteen tracks in 39 minutes, with her late father and producer [[Exaktly|d2d25ef3-32c2-4770-93fa-cc698a8871c9]] on the record. Metacritic lists it at 89 across seven reviews.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports that Pitchfork rated it 8.4 and named it Best New Music, and that the record is her first without a single thematic story. Reviews reference her processing her father's death across it.

In Range, she talks about not wanting to be consumed by the job of being an artist.

years.src: Yaya Bey: do it afraid review · Yaya Bey (Wikipedia)
years.h: Drink Sum Wtr puts out Do It Afraid
years.p: Out June 20, 2025, her first record for the label. The Line of Best Fit's John Amen gave it 8/10 and called it an ode to love.

years.cap: Yaya Bey live in studio at KEXP, Seattle, Sept. 23, 2025
yt: Full session, live on KEXP, Sept. 2025
years.h: Fidelity arrives with an essay and a short film
years.p: Lead single "Blue," then "Egyptian Musk" with NESTA. The film, "Cheers to our Fidelity," showed at Hannah Traore Gallery in New York.
years.xp: The Luna Collective reports the project is framed around three deaths: personal, communal and the loss of innocence. It also reports that she left Brooklyn and settled in D.C. because of gentrification.
